title: Feature Expansion for Graph Neural Networks
summary: The paper studies the feature space of spatial and spectral GNNs and shows that repeated aggregation makes feature subspaces linearly correlated, while weight sharing and limited node-attribute dimensionality bound representability. It proposes feature subspace flattening, which reweights each subspace independently, and structural principal components, which add a truncated SVD of the graph structure as an extra feature subspace, forming FE-GNN. Experiments on homophilic and heterophilic node classification show FE-GNN achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, e.g. 73.33% on Chameleon and an average 32% improvement over GCN on heterophilic graphs, with comparable inference time.

match_target.why: It is the user-specified Table 2 FE-GNN (C) Chameleon result, the paper's central heterophilic improvement case and the cheapest Table-2 entry to reproduce.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: no std is reported for the target (Table 2 gives a 95% CI, not std); Chameleon's 20% test split is ~455 nodes, below 2,000; accuracy is bounded, so use 2.0 absolute points.

requirements.stmt: Implement the general feature-space decomposition H = sum_t Φ_t(X, A) Θ_t, separating non-parametric feature subspaces from trainable reweighting parameters.
requirements.quote: H = GNN(X, ˆA) = T −1 X t=0 Φt(X, ˆA)Θt,

requirements.stmt: Implement FE-GNN as the sum of polynomial-filtered node-attribute subspaces plus a structural-principal-component subspace, each with independent weights.
requirements.quote: H = K X k=0 Pk(ˆL)XW (k) + SWs.

requirements.stmt: Construct S from the truncated SVD of the structural matrix, keeping principal components and singular values.
For FE-GNN (C), use Chebyshev polynomials with the recurrence P0(x)=1, P1(x)=x, Pk(x)=2xPk-1-Pk-2.
requirements.quote: Tk(x) denotes Chebyshev polynomial P0(x) = 1, P1(x) = x, Pk(x) = 2xPk−1 −Pk−2.

requirements.stmt: Apply column-wise normalization so that each column of each feature subspace contributes equally to the whole feature space.
requirements.quote: we add a column-wise normalization to ensure that each column of each feature subspace contributes equally to the whole feature space.

requirements.stmt: Keep the final FE-GNN implementation purely linear with no activation functions or dropout except for the cross-entropy loss.
requirements.quote: our implementation is purely linear without any deep artifices such as activation functions or dropout except for the cross-entropy loss

requirements.stmt: Use 94% cumulative singular values as the default truncated-SVD proportion.
requirements.quote: What proportion of the truncated SVD is appropriate? 94%.

requirements.stmt: For the target Chameleon result, use lr=0.01, weight decay=0.0005, |S|=700, hidden=64, and polynomial order k=3.
Evaluate with random 60%/20%/20% splits and report averages over 100 runs on 10 random seeds.
requirements.quote: We test on the node classification task with random 60%/20%/20% splits and summarize the results of 100 runs in Table 2

requirements.stmt: Train with Adam and early stopping using warmup 50, patience 200, and the stated maximum epoch criterion.
requirements.quote: We employ Adam for optimization and set the early stopping criteria as a warmup of 50 pluses patience of 200 for a maximum of 100 epochs.

requirements.stmt: Use the renormalized adjacency matrix with self-loops and the corresponding Laplacian as specified.
Train with the cross-entropy loss for node classification.
requirements.quote: By default, we employ the cross-entropy loss function in the node classification task

requirements.stmt: Treat the graph structure's truncated SVD as an independent feature subspace, not merely as a message-passing path.
requirements.quote: we propose to construct the expansion subspace using the truncated SVD of the structural matrix, called structural principal components

requirements.stmt: Obtain datasets through PyTorch Geometric and treat them as undirected graphs.
requirements.quote: PyG6 are employed to get these data.

requirements.stmt: Report average accuracy (micro F1 score) with a 95% confidence interval over runs.
requirements.quote: We report the average accuracy (micro F1 score) in the classification task with a 95% confidence interval in all the tables and figures.
